ex-3A01-1.title: Applying the laws of reflection
ex-3A01-1.question: A ray of light hits a plane mirror (Fig a). The angle between the incident ray and the mirror is 22°. Find the angle of reflection r and complete the ray diagram.
ex-3A01-1.answer:
i is the angle between the incident ray and the normal (Fig b).

i = 90° – 22° = 68°

By the laws of reflection, r = i = 68°

Figure c shows the complete ray diagram.

ex-3A01-3.title: Size and orientation of an image
ex-3A01-3.question:
A girl 1.4 m tall is 1 m in front of a mirror. She wears a T-shirt as shown.

(a) What is the distance between the girl’s image and the mirror?

(b) What is the height of the girl’s image?

(c) What will happen to the size of the girl’s image if the girl walks towards the mirror? Explain your answer briefly.

(d) Sketch the image of the T-shirt as seen by the girl.
ex-3A01-3.answer:
(a) Image distance = object distance = 1 m

(b) Height of image = height of girl = 1.4 m

(c) The size of the image will be unchanged since it depends only on the size of the girl, not her distance from the mirror.

ex-3A01-4.title: Location of images
ex-3A01-4.question: An object XY is placed in front of a plane mirror. In the following cases, locate the images of points X and Y. Hence draw the image of XY.
ex-3A01-4.tips:
Skill

Drawing

Drawing an image formed by a mirror

1 Draw a dotted line from a tip of the object to pass through the mirror perpendicularly.

2 Apply image distance

= object distance to

locate the image of the tip.

3 Locate the image of the other tip of the object. Join the two image points with a dotted arrow to draw the image.

Tip

When the mirror is inclined at 45°, the image of a horizontal object is vertical, and vice versa.

ex-3A01-5.title: Who can see the image?
ex-3A01-5.question: Point object O is put in front of a plane mirror. Can students A, B and C see the image of O?
ex-3A01-5.answer: ∴ A and B can see the image while C cannot.
ex-3A01-5.tips:
Tip

The position of I is independent of the position of the observer.
ex-3A01-5.think: In which direction should C move in order to see I?
ex-3A01-5.thinkAnswer: C can move upwards in the diagram, towards B, until the straight line joining C to the image I meets the reflecting part of the mirror. Equivalently, C must enter the visible region bounded by rays drawn from I through the two ends of the mirror. Moving sufficiently to the right, away from the mirror, is another possible route into this region.

ex-3A01-6.title: Position of a dressing mirror
ex-3A01-6.question:
A girl 78 cm tall stands in front of a vertical mirror (Fig a). Her eyes are

8 cm below the top of her head. She can just see her feet at the bottom edge of the mirror when she is 60 cm from it (Fig b).

(a) How high above the floor is the bottom edge of the mirror?

(b) What is the minimum length of the mirror if the girl can just see the image of her whole body in the mirror?
ex-3A01-6.answer:
By similar triangles,

H70 = 6060 + 60 = 12

H = 35 cm

The bottom edge of the mirror is 35 cm above the floor.

By similar triangles,

L78 = 6060 + 60 = 12

L = 39 cm

The minimum length of the mirror is 39 cm.

ex-3A01-7.title: Walking in front of a plane mirror
ex-3A01-7.question:
A man stands in front of a vertical plane mirror. He cannot see his shoes nor point X in the mirror. If he walks towards the mirror,

(a) can he see his shoes in the mirror?

(b) can he see point X in the mirror?
ex-3A01-7.answer:
(a)

When he walks towards the mirror, he can only see the same point on his body at the bottom edge of the mirror, so he cannot see his shoes.

(b)

When he walks towards the mirror beyond a certain point, he can see point X in the mirror.
